name: Saints Andrew Kim Taegon, Paul Chong Hasang and Companions
history: The Church in Korea was founded by lay people, scholars who found the faith in Christian books from China in the late eighteenth century. For decades it grew under persecution, often without priests, and thousands died. The 103 martyrs canonised in 1984 include Andrew Kim Taegon, the first Korean-born priest, and the lay leader Paul Chong Hasang.
life: In 1784 Yi Seung-hun, baptised in Beijing, came home to Korea and began baptising others. The young community spread the faith by itself for years and sent messengers again and again to beg for priests. Under a government that saw the new religion as a threat to the social order, it suffered waves of persecution. Paul Chong Hasang, whose father and brother had been martyred, travelled many times to Beijing to ask for clergy, and wrote a defence of the faith addressed to the authorities before his execution in 1839. Andrew Kim Taegon, son of a martyr, studied in Macau and was ordained in Shanghai in 1845. Back in Korea he served for barely a year before he was arrested and beheaded near Seoul in 1846, aged twenty-five. Among the 103 saints are French missionary bishops and priests, but most were lay men, women and children. John Paul II canonised them in Seoul in 1984.
prayerTo: Holy martyrs of Korea, you received the faith from books and handed it on with your blood. Pray for the Church in Korea, for all who must practise their faith in secret, and for me, that I may treasure the faith I received so easily and share it with courage and joy. Amen.
penance: Pray today for Christians who live under persecution, and offer a small sacrifice, such as a treat given up, for those who worship in secret.
meditation: The first Korean Catholics found Christ in the pages of a book and kept the faith alone for years. What have you done with the faith that was handed to you?
